title: Reactive Forms Setup 🧪
description: Build forms programmatically using FormGroup, FormControl, and FormBuilder.

slides.title: The Reactive Way 🎛️
slides.content:
# Form Model in the Class

With reactive forms, you define the structure and validation of the form in the component class using `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, and `FormArray`.

The template merely binds to the model using directives like `formGroup`, `formControlName`, and `formArrayName`.

Benefits:
* Immutable state – you can observe value changes as streams.
* Easier unit testing.
* Scalable for complex scenarios.

slides.title: Creating a Form Group

quizData.question: Which module must be imported for reactive forms?

slides.title: Binding in the Template
slides.content: Use `[formGroup]` and `formControlName` to link the template to the class model:
slides.codeSnippet:
<form [formGroup]="signupForm" (ngSubmit)="onSubmit()">
  <input formControlName="email" placeholder="Email">
  <input formControlName="password" type="password" placeholder="Password">
  <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
</form>

slides.title: FormBuilder – A Shorter Syntax 🛠️

quizData.question: The service that simplifies reactive form creation is called ________.
quizData.explanation: Inject `FormBuilder` and use `fb.group()` for cleaner form creation.

slides.title: Value Changes & Status Changes 📡
slides.content:
You can subscribe to the form’s `valueChanges` or `statusChanges` observables to react to user input:

```typescript
this.signupForm.valueChanges.subscribe(val => console.log(val));
```

This is extremely powerful for real‑time validation, auto‑save, or dependent fields.
